article_lead.description: an unnormalised prior weight that can still give a valid posterior when the data make its normalising integral finite

new_bank_questions.title: A boundary left by an improper prior
new_bank_questions.body: A binomial success probability has prior weight $w(\theta)\propto[\theta(1-\theta)]^{-1}$. For five trials, determine the posterior kernel and whether it is proper (a) if two trials succeed and (b) if none succeed. Give the posterior mean in the proper case.
new_bank_questions.answer: For two successes, the kernel is $\theta^{2-1}(1-\theta)^{3-1}$, hence the proper $\operatorname{Beta}(2,3)$ posterior has mean $2/(2+3)=0.4$. With no successes, the kernel is $\theta^{-1}(1-\theta)^4$; its integral diverges at zero, so there is no posterior probability distribution.
